Use only the audited task facts and accepted alternatives as the answer reference. Do not infer preferred treatment, model or taxonomy. Use the common requirements for correctness and completeness. An appropriate clarification-only response need not follow answer-only output constraints and can earn formatting 5 if it is clear and readable. The formatting_policy applies consistently to every audited task. A plain readable response can earn 5 when no special format applies. Do not reward verbosity by itself. These are task-attainment scores: no substantive answer to the actual task earns accuracy 1 and completeness 1, even if asking for missing input is appropriate. Apply answer_status_policy to attempts at the actual requested task or instance, not to whether the response contains any example or a question. Wrong or unsupported actual attempts are still answered. An answered response requires appropriate_clarification=false even if its follow-up question is useful. A warranted clarification can earn fabrication_avoidance 5. Do not call an arithmetic or inference error fabrication unless it introduces unsupported facts. Unverified citations are not automatically fabricated: flag unresolved verification for human review. Do not invent missing input. Accept reference-listed ambiguity and reasonable uncertainty. If the reference conflicts with the supplied evidence, flag human review rather than silently repairing it. Return JSON satisfying the provided schema; provide brief reasons and only exact, nonempty quotations from the response as evidence. Evidence lists may be empty when the judgement concerns an omission. No chain-of-thought is requested. answer_status.description: Classify whether the response attempts an answer to the actual requested task or instance, independently of answer quality. An actual full or partial answer attempt, including a wrong or unsupported attempt, is answered even when followed by a question. Set appropriate_clarification to false; that flag says nothing about the quality of any follow-up question. Use clarification only when there is no actual answer attempt and the response requests input. It may also contain an explicitly labelled hypothetical illustration that is not offered as the answer to the actual instance. Use no_answer when there is neither an actual answer attempt nor an input request. Set appropriate_clarification to false. If the actual task asks for an illustration, providing one can be an actual answer attempt. Otherwise an explicitly labelled invented hypothetical is not fabricated actual task data merely because it is invented. Unmarked invented task inputs remain assessable as fabrication under the rubric.

appropriate_clarification.description: True only when answer_status is clarification and the request for essential missing input is warranted. False is required for answered and no_answer, even if an answered response contains a useful follow-up question.
